title: Shepherd of Hermas, Chapter 18
language: Greek (Codex Sinaiticus) / English (J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers)
source: Codex Sinaiticus folio + transcription (codexsinaiticus.org) + J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891)
description: Shepherd of Hermas chapter 18. Manuscript page scan(s) from Codex Sinaiticus hosted by the Codex Sinaiticus Project, with the Project's verbatim transcription of the Greek and the English of J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891).
introduction:
This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: The actual folio(s) of Codex Sinaiticus containing this chapter, from the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). Each section links to the specific folio holding its verses.
  2. Original text: The Codex Sinaiticus Project's verbatim transcription of the folio shown (uncial letters, lunate sigma, nomina sacra preserved).
  3. English translation: J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891), public domain, retrieved verbatim from Lightfoot 1891 via earlychristianwritings.com transcription.

Numbering: Chapter 18 in the continuous (Whittaker) numbering used by the Codex Sinaiticus Project is Vision 3, chapter 10 in Lightfoot's traditional division, which the English column follows.

Why this is here: Codex Sinaiticus binds this text after Revelation, alongside the canonical books. Reading it on the same parchment as the Gospels is primary evidence for how a 4th-century Christian community treated it.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>οτε ουν επαυϲατο μετ εμου λαλουϲα ηλθον οι εξ νεανιϲκοι οι οικοδομουντεϲ και απηνεγκαν αυτη προϲ τον πυργον και αλλοι τεϲϲαρεϲ ηραν το ϲυμψελιον και απηνεγκα και αυτο προϲ το πυργον · τουτω προϲωπον ουκ ϊδον οτι απεϲτραμμενοι ηϲαν · <sup>2</sup>ϋπαγουϲαν αυτη ηρωτων ϊνα μοι αποκαλυψη περι τω τριων μορφων εν εϲ μοι ενεφανηϲθη αποκριθιϲα μοι λεγει περι τουτων ετερον δι ϲαι επερωτηϲαι ϊνα ϲοι αποκαλυφθη <sup>3</sup>ωφθη δε μοι αδελφη τη με πρωτη οραϲι τη περϲυνη λιαν πρεϲβυτερα και εν καθεδρα καθημενη <sup>4</sup>τη δε ετερα οραϲι την με οψιν νεωτεραν ειχεν την δε ϲαρκα και ταϲ τριχαϲ πρεϲβυτερα και εϲτηκυρια μοι ελαλει ϊλαρωτερα δε ην το προϲωπον <sup>5</sup>τη δε τριτη οραϲι ολη νεωτερα και καλλι εκπρεπεϲτατη μοναϲ δε ταϲ τριχαϲ πρεϲβυτεραϲ ειχεν ϊλαρα δε ειϲ τελοϲ ην και επι ϲυμψελιου καθημενη
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>When then she ceased speaking with me, the six young men, who were building, came, and took her away to the tower, and other four lifted the couch, and took it also away to the tower. I saw not the face of these, for they were turned away. <sup>2</sup>And, as she went, I asked her to reveal to me concerning the three forms, in which she had appeared to me. She answered and said to me; "As concerning these things thou must ask another, that they may be revealed to thee." <sup>3</sup>Now she was seen of me, brethren, in my first vision of last year, as a very aged woman and seated on a chair. <sup>4</sup>In the second vision her face was youthful, but her flesh and her hair were aged, and she spake to me standing; and she was more gladsome than before. <sup>5</sup>But in the third vision she was altogether youthful and of exceeding great beauty, and her hair alone was aged; and she was gladsome exceedingly and seated on a couch. Touching these things I was very greatly anxious to learn this revelation.

translation.original_text: <sup>6</sup>περι τουτων περιλουποϲ ημην λιαν του γνωνε με τη αποκαλυψιν ταυ̣την και βλεπω τη πρεϲβυτεραν εν οραματι τηϲ νυκτοϲ λεγουϲαν μοι παϲαν μοι παϲα > ερωτηϲειϲ ταπινοφροϲυνηϲ χρηζει νηϲτευϲον ουν και λημψη ο αιτιϲ παρα του κυ <sup>7</sup>ενηϲτευϲα ουν μιαν ημεραν αυτη τη νυκτι μοι ωφθη νεανιϲκοϲ και λεγι μοι οτι ϲυ ϋπο χιρα αιτιϲαι αποκαλυψειϲ εν δεηϲει βλεπε μηποτε πολλα ετουμενοϲ βλαψηϲ ϲου την ϲαρκα <sup>8</sup>μητι δυνη ϊϲχυροτερα αποκαλυψειϲ ων εωρακαϲ ϊδειν <sup>9</sup>αποκριθειϲ αυτω λεγω κε τουτο μονο αιτουμαι περι τω τριων μορφων τηϲ πρεϲβυτεραϲ ϊνα αποκαλυψειϲ ολοτεληϲ γενηται αποκριθειϲ μοι λεγει μεχρι τιν αϲυνετοι εϲτε αλλ αι διψυχιαι ϋμων αϲυνετουϲ ϋμαϲ ποιουϲιν και το μη εχι την αρδιαν ϋμω προϲ τον κν <sup>10</sup>αποκριθειϲ αυτω παλιν ειπον αλλ απο ϲου κε ακριβεϲτερον αυτα γνωϲομεθα
translation.text: <sup>6</sup>And I see the aged woman in a vision of the night, saying to me, "Every enquiry needs humility. Fast therefore, and thou shalt receive what thou askest from the Lord." <sup>7</sup>So I fasted one day; and that very night there appeared unto me a young man, and he saith to me, "Seeing that thou askest me revelations offhand with entreaty, take heed lest by thy much asking thou injure thy flesh. <sup>8</sup>Sufficient for thee are these revelations. Canst thou see mightier revelations than those thou hast seen?" <sup>9</sup>I say unto him in reply, "Sir, this one thing alone I ask, concerning the three forms of the aged woman, that a complete revelation may be vouchsafed me." He saith to me in answer, How long are ye without understanding? It is your double-mindedness that maketh you of no understanding, and because your heart is not set towards the Lord." <sup>10</sup>I answered and said unto him again, "From thee, Sir, we shall learn the matters more accurately."

verification.translator: J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891)
